previous_findings_closed: 1 (medium) deferred_page_boundary guard: closed. build.py:351-387 now requires all of the following. The flag is exactly True. The continuation has no conditions and no condition scope is open. The continuation is on current_page with page_start False. The immediately preceding segment has conditions, is marked, and has no condition_end_corresp. The scan change happens inside that segment (transition > 0), and every fragment from the transition to the end of that segment is on the new scan. The on-page fragments seen so far in the unit equal exactly that tail, so a unit that starts mid-page or has an intervening segment fails. The transition fragment's printed_page equals the continuation's. No page_start True fragment exists on the page, and no earlier deferral exists on the page. Some cases are rejected implicitly. A preceding 'transclude' segment never advances current_page, so the scan check rejects it. A page that starts at a clause's first fragment fails transition > 0, but that case is already handled by the pre-conditional pb at line 388. I traced all five required negatives in test_page_start_inside_optional_clause_can_be_deferred_once (lines 864-877). mid_page fails because transition == 0 and on_page holds the unit's first fragment. intervening_unconditional fails because the preceding segment has no conditions. wrong_page fails the current-page check. wrong_label fails the printed_page match. non_true fails 'is not True'. The three earlier negatives (page_start True duplicate, conditioned continuation, repeated deferral) are kept. The positive case gives pb n=['1','2'], facs n1, and the pb comes after j:endConditional.

notes: This approves code only. It accepts no batch, source words, minted identities, generated output, order or export.

deferred_page_boundary_approved is true for the narrowed contract: the transition is inside the immediately preceding marked, self-contained conditional segment, and the deferred segment is the first segment after it.

Non-blocking: if the preceding clause has a repeat_cue, its navigation note is emitted after j:endConditional but before the deferred pb, so the facsimile puts the cue on the earlier page. One extra guard condition, `not preceding.get('repeat_cue')`, would rule this out. Otherwise check it per use (see integration checks).

Non-blocking: the check `preceding_fragments[transition-1]['scan'] != current_page` is always true, because transition is the first index on current_page. It does no harm. The real 'different earlier scan' guarantee comes from transition > 0.
Non-blocking: when both printed_page values are None, the label match passes and the pb is emitted without @n. This suits unnumbered leaves.

Non-blocking: test_integrated_source_baseline_matches_fixed_importer_fixture only runs when some unit has canonical_parts, while the build gate fires on a wider set of triggers. Running it when `'accepted_literal_baseline' in readings` or the build gate predicate is true would keep the two copies tied together in every case.
